org.name: His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service

hazard: Continued prevalence of New Psychoactive Substances and inadequate staffing of Substance Misuse Team

concerns.quote: That there is no proper provision for the care and supervision of prisoners who present with complex physical and/or mental health needs
concerns.hazard: lack of proper care and supervision of prisoners with complex physical and mental health needs

concerns.quote: That at present, if a prisoner is assessed as needing a four person unlock, and is within the Segregation Unit, there are insufficient prison staff to provide him with a proper regime and to unlock him after lunchtime
concerns.hazard: insufficient prison staff to provide proper regime and unlock prisoners in segregation

concerns.quote: That the use of New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) remains rife within the prison, and presentations such as Mr [name redacted] are not diminishing, and that the Substance Misuse Team requires further staff to be effective in future
concerns.hazard: continued prevalence of New Psychoactive Substances and inadequate staffing of Substance Misuse Team

concerns.quote: That the documentary tool for decision making between prison staff and healthcare staff, as to whether a prisoner is fit to remain in Segregation and should do so, is unclear in design or in use
concerns.hazard: unclear documentary tool for decision making between prison staff and healthcare staff regarding segregation fitness

concerns.quote: That healthcare staff are insufficiently alert to the issue that physical symptoms which require urgent medical attention may be occluded by mental health issues
concerns.hazard: insufficient alertness of healthcare staff to physical symptoms occluded by mental health issues

reports.title: Oliver Mulangala: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

concerns.quote: The availability and use of illicit drugs posed a threat to the stability of the prison, contributing to debt, bullying and fear. The positive drug testing rate at HMP High Down was among the highest in adult male prisons
The availability of illicit substances continued to be a serious concern that undermined safety and stability. The rate of positive drug tests remained as high as at our full inspection in 2023
It's probably easier to get [REDACTED] or a mobile phone in here than it is to get sugar. I think some prisoners may get coerced and groomed into taking it and running up debts
[REDACTED] is a daily occurrence, it's too much to handle...some batches are bad and they can then be violent
nearly every day when someone is found under the influence of NPS (New psychoactive substances)
If they have access to a phone it makes it easier for them to obtain drugs

prisoners were able to get possession of smart phones (even though they are not allowed to have them), and that having access to smart phones enabled prisoners to arrange for contraband to be delivered into prison, threaten and coerce, communicate across different prisons, and take and share video footage within the prison
[REDACTED] defence technology exists to detect, track [REDACTED] and identify
The Office of National Statistics recorded, however, that between 2008 and 2019 there were 145 drug-related deaths in UK prisons, which equates to an average of 13.2 pa over that 11-year period

The 6th Report of the House of Commons Justice Committee states that between December 2022 and December 2024 there were 136 drug-related deaths in UK prisons, which equates to 68 death per year in that 2-year period, in other words about one every 5 days
(1) New psychoactive substances, especially [REDACTED] , are easily available in HM Prison High Down, as in many other prisons in England & Wales
(2) Mobile phones are easily available in HM Prison High Down, as in many other prisons in England & Wales
